- **Phase 2b (code):** verify row t samples its own token with the full chain from its logits (Philox(seed, pos0+t)); the
  serve loop accepts drafts while `window[a+1] == outv[a]` and emits outv[0..a] (the first mismatch = a target draw).
  The MTP drafter proposes its argmax (mtp.cpp: sp.greedy = true) → q is a point mass → this sample-and-match rule IS the
  standard speculative accept/resample rule (accept d with min(1, p(d)/q(d)) = p(d); on reject, resample from
  (p − q)+ ∝ p without d). Uniforms: one per position; a rejected row's draw is re-used by the next window at the same
  position but never decided anything kept (a depends only on rows ≤ a) → exact. Seeds: steady_clock ns per request.

- **Cause of the Stop delay (server.py):** keep-alives go out once per prompt chunk (PP line, ~3.9 s per 8,192 tokens);
  a write to a closed socket usually fails only on the 2nd try → STOP reaches the engine 2–3 chunks late (the engine checks
  should_stop per chunk). **Fix (r5b e8d17f9 / r5 9b765d2):** watch_disconnect() polls the connection (MSG_PEEK, 0.25 s)
  while streaming; on close: cancel + STOP at once, only for the request the engine is running (a queued request must not
  stop another; a cancelled queued request never starts), once per request. Unit test: fires on close, silent while open.
  **Two-tab fix** = round 4's r4-web patch (applies cleanly; esprima + QuickJS 15/15) → r5b 75c947b / r5 f02d33c.
  FAIL5 + BR3 queued before the llama.cpp block. R5-web.shared-settings.json = copy of your Cstar4 file (temp 1.0).

### 12:45 — PHASE A RESULTS + DECISION POINT (Phase A used ~50 min of its ≤5 h)
**What upstream already does on the prompt path (v0.1.24, read in src/prefill/prefill.cpp):** 8192-token chunks
(`--prefill auto`, lending cache slots); every non-resident expert of every layer streamed in a fixed order through a
384-slot DMA ring while the attention halves run (96 slots + host-copy threads when < 90 % of the arena is pinned);
MMQ grouped expert GEMMs straight on the GGUF blocks (16 experts per launch, all 48 layers of this model), with a
per-expert gather into a contiguous group buffer; batched layer-1 PLE + next-chunk n-gram read-ahead on a 64-thread
reader; tensor-core QSA prompt attention (0.1.22) and selection (0.1.24); one host sync per MoE layer (grouping).
**Where a cold uncached 32K prompt's time goes** (untraced, STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING, first start of the CLI = includes
~0.55 s of first-use kernel loading in "embed+steps"; GPU busy 10.74 of 10.91 s): expert work 42 % = MMQ gate/up 13.5 +
down 7.5 (≈1.4 TFLOPS: ~160 rows per expert per 8192-chunk = underfilled) + the per-expert group gather 9.9 ("dequant"
label) + combine 3.8 + router/shared 2.3 + **waiting for expert copies 3.9 %** (= weight movement is NOT the limiter);
mixers: GDN 24.5 %, QSA 14 % (selection 2.2 % at 32K → 5.6 % at 112K), hyper-connection reads 12 %. 112K: same shares.
nsys (traced, 17.2 s vs 11.0 untraced — nsys inflates the prompt path) confirms the order. 120K 2-chunk slice at depth
(chunks 11–12): logs/r6/prof/nsys-pp112k-c11.*.
**Decode (nsys, 120 windows):** per layer CPU pool 140 µs, GPU working beside it 72.5 µs (52 %), GPU phase flag→doorbell
187 µs (GDN) / 222 µs (QSA); GPU flag-wait (exposed CPU) 3.16 ms of a 17.9 ms traced window = 16 %. Exposure is uneven:
layers 0–7 carry 1.36 of 3.25 ms (layer 0 pool 439 µs), layers 15–37 mostly hidden. Tail 0.84, commit 0.52, MTP 1.12 ms.
**Item 2 (router→CPU start):** no sync/readback delay — the doorbell kernel runs right after the router top-10 (ids,
weights, x to mapped memory), the host spin-polls it; serial host work before the workers start = plan 1.0 + activation
quantize 6.9 + jobs 2.8 µs per layer (10.7 µs; 0.51 ms/window). Exact overlap of it: ≤ ~0.25 ms/window where exposed.
**Item 3 (helper, measured, exact greedy windows, meas build):** per layer helper launch 4.9–7.9 µs, CPU pool 136.5
vs 165.6 µs, wait for the helper after the pool 4.1–8.9 µs; helper serves 5 % of entries. **The 8 GiB pin cap is the whole
story:** with it (upstream default whenever a helper is on, "Windows workaround" in the comment but applied on Linux)

  is never cleared between requests; a Stop during a prompt read leaves it "cancelled" (Prefill::run should_stop). 0.1.26
  changed the per-chunk draft-layer hook to `if (!e.empty() || …) return false;` with `e` = that string → the next
  request's first batched chunk fails → `ERR cancelled` → main returns 1. v0.1.24's hook ignored `e`. Short prompts
  (read by windows) do not go through the hook, which is why round 5's stop120k test (short follow-up) would not see it.
  **Fix = patch 0013** (r7-port 13d2c41): draft_kv gets its own error string in both hooks (serve + generate); no
  arithmetic change. patches/r7 now 13; r7-meas and r7-oracle rebased onto it. Queued: stop_repro.py (Stop during a 32K

  floor: ++T` with dprob = the drafter's RAW probability, so **the floor gates draft 1 too** (T = 1 windows exist; A.1 saw
  them). Re-run with the real rule (work/r8/policy2.py; W(1) = W(2) − 3.9 ms ≈ 12.1 ms, estimated; ±1 ms moves results by

- **Prompt group copies, source read** (prefill.cpp compute(), moe_mmq.cu gather_native): the 'dequant' bucket (1,065 ms =
  10.4 % of a 32K prompt's GPU time; 3.7 s at 112K) is a PLAIN COPY kernel per expert (gate | up → group gate/up slot,
  down → group down slot; GGUF blocks unchanged for a native pack), 11.9 µs per ~2.1 MB expert, run after the H2D DMA
  into a ring slot (the wait is the separate 'wait copy' bucket: the timer events bracket only the copy kernel). MMQ
  already takes a per-expert stride (Product::expert_bytes) → the gather can go entirely: DMA each blob straight into
  ring slots laid out as the MMQ group (16 consecutive slots, stride = MAXBLOB + 4 KiB, each blob RIGHT-aligned in its
  slot so the down matrix's ≤ 1-tile over-read always lands in that slot's never-written zero pad), resident experts
  copied D2D into their slot (8.5 % of experts), slots released after the group's down GEMM instead of after the gather.
  Same weights bytes, same activations, same groups → bit-identical expected. Ceiling 10.4 % of prompt GPU time (−1.07 s
  at 32K, −3.7 s at 112K); risk: the copy engine (188 GB per 32K prompt ≈ 18 GB/s today) may become the limit.

### Phase B (started 22:45 while the A.6 screens finish; base frozen = r8-port 3c8eaf6, C\*8's tree)
- **Track 1 = PR245** (branch r8-pr245 daed1cf; patches/r8-B/0013; engine-r8p sha b40e3fe5…; results/r8/builds.md R8p):
  parity + exact + served A/B done (above); TF on the measurement twin (r8-meas-pr245, engine-r8pm) queued.
- **Track 2 = MMQ expert pointers** (branch r8-mmqptr 8fc285d on r8-port; worktree strata-r8s; engine-r8s):
  * mmq.cuh's three expert-offset sites take `x` as a table of per-expert pointers when stride_channel_x < 0. The
    pinned llama.cpp checkout is NOT touched: CMake copies ggml-cuda's headers into the build tree and edits mmq.cuh
    there, checking that all three sites matched (else a warning and the gather stays). A full copy next to the
    original is impossible (quantize.cuh / mmq-load-tiles.cuh include "mmq.cuh" by sibling path).
  * prefill: in stream-all chunks, each streamed blob is DMA'd to the END of its ring slot (slot = MAXBLOB + 4 KiB tail,
    zeroed at every prompt's start: borrowed cache memory), so the down matrix's ≤ 1-tile over-read always meets
    zeros. A per-layer table [gate/up | down pointer per routed expert] is written into the mapped grouping table and
    copied by a kernel (a cudaMemcpyAsync would queue behind the copy stream's blobs). Resident experts (8.5 %) are
    still gathered into the group buffer, with a zeroed tail after their down matrix. A streamed slot is held until
    the group's down product is queued, then released, and give_back never passes the first held entry.
  * deadlock guard: a group reads in place only if its slots lie within half the ring; a group spread wider (a prompt
    routed to few experts, e.g. one repeated token) gathers as before. Same groups either way → same launches and
    stream-k split → bit-identical expected. STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ_PTRS=0 = the gather (A/B in one binary).
  * tests queued: exact CLI pairs (fixed cache 3500, greedy, 64 new tokens) at 2K, 32K, 112K and two repeated-token
    prompts (4K, 9K: the fallback path), on vs off, with group counts; then alternating timing pairs at 32K / 112K.
- **Track 2 results (engine-r8s 8fc285d; STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ_PTRS default vs =0, fixed cache 3500, greedy):**
  * **exact: output identical on vs off** at 2K (3e219376), 32K (651f56c8), 112K (b806e832), repeated-token 4K
    (5864a284) and 9K (b1a6073b); groups read in place: 2K 1,373 of 1,373; 32K 6,079 of 6,079; rep4k 798 of 798.
    The repeated-token prompts still route to ~270 experts per layer, so the wide-span fallback never triggered →

  * **speed, untimed alternating pairs: 32K 10.15 / 10.15 → 10.04 / 10.06 s (−1.0 %); 112K 34.37 / 34.38 → 33.99 /

- **Mechanism found (source, generate.cpp ~3954 / 5754):** the adaptive tier makes swapped-in experts resident only
  when a NON-BLOCKING `cudaEventQuery(adapt_ev)` says the copy has landed; until then (and for the evicted expert at
  once) the CPU computes them. So WHICH round first computes a swapped expert on the GPU depends on copy timing →
  CPU-vs-GPU float order differs for that expert in that round (the engine's own note: "a GPU expert and the CPU's
  compute the same quantized expert with different float order, so a near-tie can flip … perplexity equal") →
  rounding-level, timing-dependent divergence — pre-existing in Strata (C\*8 has it too); PR245's faster GPU kernels
  move the timing, they do not change any arithmetic (bitwise kernels, sanitizer-clean). Matches the data: divergence
  starts mid-text at one token with a small NLL change (0.2756 vs 0.2816) that grows through the recurrent state.
  TF matrix with the tier ON, single long64k, 12 runs so far ({both, pointers off, old experts, neither} × 3):
  **all identical to C\*8** (rare event). Repeats with --adapt-swaps 0 (fixed computation) queued on both twins.

- 11:10–11:40 **Phase A.1 prep (code only, no GPU): exact speculative sampling** — branch r9-ess (worktree strata-r9e,
  from r9-pr245 = C\*10's tree); switch STRATA_SPEC_EXACT=1 (core/spec_exact.hpp). Design:
  * drafter: the coupled path's chain (penalties from the ring, top_k / top_p / min_p / temperature over the draft head's
    subset) → the final distribution q as EXACT integer counts out of 2^24 (the bucket each entry owns under the 24-bit
    inverse-CDF walk: C(c) = clamp(ceil(c·2^24)), so q is literally the distribution the draw has); the draft is drawn
    with a PROPOSAL stream (Philox counter + (1 << 48), at the verifying row's counter); q's list (≤ 64 ids + counts) goes
    to a device buffer per step; the gate value stays today's (raw argmax probability, computed BEFORE the draw:
    greedy argmax + row_top_prob on the raw logits) and the raw argmax token is kept for the lookup check;
  * verify head (sample_tokens_spec, split top_k + a new merge kernel): a row with a draft x accepts iff
    floor(u64·Q(x)/2^64) < P(x) (ACCEPTANCE stream, P and Q the integer counts; error < 2^-64), else draws from the
    residual max(P − Q, 0) over the target's list (RESIDUAL stream; never empty after a rejection: both sum to 2^24 and
    Q(x) > P(x); never holds x); a row without a draft (the bonus) = `sampled_tail_warp` itself (today's stream and
    uniform → bit-identical to today's draw); lookup drafts = point masses (q = 1 at x);
  * host: the accept rule (window[t+1] == out[t]) is unchanged; the lookup-vs-MTP choice compares the lookup's first token
    with the drafter's RAW argmax (before its draw), never with the sampled draft (else the choice of q at position 1
    would depend on that position's own draw); draft length = today's rule on the raw top probability (before the draw).
  * test harness work/r9/ess_test.cu (the real kernels; round 8's tiny-vocab cases + the chain + K from q + lookup point
    masses + the negative control; chi-square of the first token and the first two; bonus row = sample_tokens bit for

- **Phase A prep, more branches (code only):**
  * **A.2 r9-nosync** (worktree strata-r9s, 1c5193b; engine-r9s built 11:18): the decode loops' commit no longer waits
    for its graph (`Verifier::commit(n, err, defer_wait)` + `settle()` at the end of a request; STRATA_COMMIT_SYNC=1 =
    the old wait). Why it is safe: the commit graph writes GDN state/conv, the QSA indexers and the PLE history; the
    drafter's round graph reads only the window's final residuals (written by run()) and its own K/V; the next window
    is ordered behind the commit on the verifier's (non-blocking) stream; nothing else reads the session until the
    request ends (settle). The prompt's windows keep the wait.
  * **A.8 r9-adet** (worktree strata-r9d, 98b2ec3): STRATA_ADAPT_LAND=N lands the adaptive tier's swaps before the N-th
    window after the one that issued them (blocking only if a copy is still running) instead of on a non-blocking
    event query. The swap DECISIONS are already deterministic (usage counts are not written while the thread ranks
    them). The TF loop (MEASUREMENT commit) has its own apply_pending and needs the same change in a measurement twin.

- 03:45 **A.2 coded** (branch r11-a2 6940855, `STRATA_ROUTER_Q8K=1`, off by default): the doorbell kernel becomes one
  block per 256-value superblock (n_tok × 10 blocks) that copies its floats as before AND writes ggml's Q8_K block
  (`quantize_row_q8_K_ref` bit for bit: first largest |x| sets the sign, iscale = −127/max by `__fdiv_rn`, round half
  to even of the IEEE product, int bsums, d = 1/iscale; ggml-base is compiled without -march, so its multiply and the
  magic-number rounding are separate operations) into mapped memory; the last block rings (device counter per token
  group). The dispatch then takes those rows for every layer whose gate/up activation is Q8_K (all 48 here) and skips
  its input quantization (0.29 ms per window on LDR). Parity test work/r11/tests/q8k_parity.cu links the build's
  libggml-base.a and compares byte for byte (Gaussian rows at 4 scales, |max| ties of both signs, a zero block,
  denormals, huge values). Queued: build + parity on both cards.

  test row (max |x| 2.1e-38: −127/max overflows to −inf): ggml's magic-number rounding turns ±inf / NaN into 0 (x86's
  default NaN 0xFFC00000), the GPU's `__float2int_rn` into 127. Now the kernel does ggml's nearest_int bit for bit (the
  1.5·2^23 add, x86's NaN result) and sums the stored int8 values into bsums → **0 of 5,120 blocks differ on both
  cards** (branch r11-a2 7aea44a, engine-r11a2 012484d0…).

    killed a kernel. **Both GPUs here have the kernel execution timeout on** (cuDeviceGetAttribute
    KERNEL_EXEC_TIMEOUT = 1 for the 5080 and the 4060 Ti: the X server is attached to both), so any single kernel that
    runs past it (seconds) is killed. The error surfaced at the prompt path's check, so the kernel may be any earlier
    one on that stream — e.g. a device-side spin wait (the engine waits on host / copy flags inside kernels) during a
    host stall. MemAvailable stayed ≥ 25.4 GiB. 0.1.39's server restarted the engine by itself: that request got an
    empty reply, the next one waited ~12 s, the chat cache was lost. One occurrence in all of this round's and earlier
    logs. Not caused by #693 (old arm). **For you: if the 5080 did not have the X server attached, its kernels would not
    be under the watchdog — your call, a system change; noted for the REPORT and the backlog** (engine side: bounded
    spins that give up and relaunch instead of spinning past the watchdog).

- **A8 — where the cost of an extra token goes (Phase 0 item 2, LDR MTP windows):** T1 → T4 adds 7.30 ms per window:
  the GPU waiting for the CPU pool 3.74 (51 %), GPU experts 2.13 (29 %), mixers 0.56 (8 %), HC reads + router 0.52
  (7 %), the draft round's T-row front 0.34 (5 %), head 0.06. The two big parts are expert weight READS: the CPU pool
  streams ~360 MB per window from DRAM at ~74 of ~77 GB/s (Round 11), the GPU's VRAM-hit kernels read the newly routed
  VRAM experts. No exact change reduces those bytes; what can change is WHEN the CPU reads them. **The draft round
  (nsys of a sampled run, ~1.6 ms GPU for a round with 3 steps, 211 kernels): draft head Q6_K 19 %, the draft layer's
  small projections 17 %, the exact sampler over 40,525 logits 14 % (74 µs per step), HC reads 10 %, the rest < 6 %
  each; host 0.01 ms.** My three ideas, each with its paper estimate and kill number written BEFORE its data:
  * **A8-1 next-layer RAM warming (exact):** while the GPU runs layer l+1's mixer + HC read (~0.15 ms per layer, ~7 ms
    per window) the CPU pool and the DRAM are idle; the engine's own next-layer router lookahead (CS-T's
    RouterLookahead: layer l+1's router on layer l's MoE input, today only for the file tier) predicts layer l+1's
    experts at layer l's start; the idle workers would read the predicted CPU-side experts into the caches (~11 MB
    of DRAM time per layer fits that phase; a layer's ~4 CPU-side experts are ~7.6 MB), and layer l+1's pool would
    compute them from cache. Arithmetic unchanged (which bytes are cached only). **Paper estimate:** per layer, pool'
    = pool × (1 − r + r·c) with r = the in-time recall of CPU-side experts (bytes ≈ count) and c = cached / DRAM time
    per expert; exposed wait' = max(0, pool' − (pool − waitCPU)); saving = Σ (waitCPU − wait'). Inputs to measure:
    r (measurement build r12-look: STRATA_R12_LOOKREC=1 runs the lookahead and counts, warms nothing) and c
    (work/r12/tests/hotcold.cpp: ggml's own one-token dot products on this model's expert shapes, 15 pinned workers,
    DRAM vs cached). **Kill: predicted saving under 3 % of the LDR round (0.54 ms of 17.9 ms per window).**
  * **A8-2 an exact faster draft sampler:** 74 µs per draft step for the chain over 40,525 logits; a top-20 select
    could take ~10 µs, but the saving is ≤ 0.064 ms × 2.29 steps per round = 0.15 ms per LDR round = 0.8 %. **Kill:
    under 1 % → DEAD on paper.**
  * **A8-3 an L3-resident hot set across windows (exact: non-temporal loads for experts not reused):** prize =
    exposed CPU wait × (share of a window's CPU-side bytes that were CPU-side in the previous window at the same layer
    and fit in the V-cache CCD's 96 MB) × (1 − c). Input: the A1R routing dump. **Kill: under 3 % of the LDR round.**

- ~22:10 **Splice C's prompt read, split (your addition 1; results/r15/s3-prompt-split-q5s-C.md, work/r15/s3_prompt_split.py):**
  the split caps the prompt chunk at **1,024 tokens** (the 8 GB 4060 Ti has room for 431 cache slots; a 16K chunk would
  borrow all of them; the engine warns "#448"), so every 1,024 tokens the 5080 re-reads the experts outside the 72 GiB
  RAM budget from the SSD: **120K prompt = 1.28 TB from the drive at 5.4 GB/s.** The 5080 stage is the critical path
  (236.0 of 236.8 s at 120K; 62.7 of 63.7 at 32K): **expert uploads ~50 %**, dequant 16–19 %, expert GEMMs ~11 %,
  attention/GDN/other ~13 %, host grouping 3 %, KV staging 3–7 %. The 4060 Ti stage (layer 47 + head) is busy ~20 %
  of the read, overlapped (its own uploads about half of that); the link (hand-off copies) ≤ 0.6 % (≤ 1.35 s at 120K).
  → step 5's chunk options: --prefill auto:32768 / auto:8192 would be no-ops (the engine caps any chunk at what every
  stage can lend), so they became explicit 2,048 and 512, and the split points 46 and 44 (40 likely leaves the 8 GB
  card no room); each arm records the chunk/split the engine actually ran; a no-op is reported after one arm.
